A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IHRUT research, and their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains an appendix or the separately referenced Supplemental Document.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 2–4 report original reconstruction experiments on synthetic HSOD-BIT and Houston data, real LASIS calibration data, and component ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original reconstruction experiments and reports revised noise-model comparisons and additional data-module ablations in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the degradation model, calibration and synthesis procedure, SPE attention, adaptive momentum module and cross-stage prior module. The additional module configurations in Table 5 are experimental alternatives to the unchanged proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HSOD-BIT for training and evaluate six synthetic HSOD-BIT scenes, one Houston scene and three real LASIS calibration scenes. The revised ablations remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: The reconstruction comparators in Table 2 are unchanged. V2 removes Table 4's whole-network channel-attention replacement and introduces three CA/SPE data-module alternatives and two alternative momentum configurations in Table 5, including one described as resembling previously cited methods.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces controlled configurations testing attention placement and momentum-branch wiring within five-stage IHRUT. The existing data format, splits, preprocessing, 300-epoch training protocol and evaluation metrics in Section 4.1 are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 retains the progressive component ablation but replaces the global channel-attention comparison with more targeted attention and momentum tests in Table 5 and Figure 5. Table 3 also revises the noise-model comparison to distinguish standard noise from the proposed pixel-wise model. These refine existing diagnostic questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and scene averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2 introduces no experimental uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 is unchanged. Table 3 reports Standard Noise at 38.82/0.987 in place of v1's G plus Nshot entry at 38.16/0.974; this does not establish a same-setting improvement. The 38.76/0.984 global-CA result is removed, while Table 5 adds five alternatives scoring 38.31–38.66 dB. V2's claimed 0.64 dB advantage for m6 conflicts with Table 3's 39.28−38.82=0.46 dB.

T1.justification: The physical assumptions, calibration derivations and unfolding equations (1)–(13) are unchanged. Table 5's formulas specify experimental configurations without adding a formal result or revising the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: realistic degradation-based data synthesis and an effective, lightweight IHRUT reconstruction network. Additional ablations support these retained claims without expanding their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 shifts from interpreting progressive SPE additions and a global channel-attention penalty to arguing that attention placement and two successive weighting operations explain advantages over alternative momentum configurations. No substantive applicability boundary or limitation is added.

D1.justification: V2's abstract adds a code repository link absent from v1, and Table 5 explicitly documents the tested data-module formulas. Existing implementation, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. Repository contents and accessibility are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references covering topics including STEM noise calibration, infrared/RGB conversion, image restoration and hyperspectral super-resolution, modestly expanding Sections 2.2–2.3. Table 5 also connects a momentum alternative to previously cited work. The main novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Sections 4.2 and 4.4 receive localized rewrites, related-work passages expand, and author contact information and acknowledgements are added. The section sequence and most of the narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and replaces Figure 5 with a 20× error-map comparison of the new variants. It reorders and relabels Table 3, removes a row and relocates Table 4, and updates Figure 2's thumbnails while moving it from page 3 to page 4. The overall layout is retained.

improvement.justification: Table 5 provides more targeted evidence about attention placement and momentum weighting than v1's single global channel-attention replacement, and the new code link improves access documentation. These are modest gains with the main method and benchmark results unchanged. They are tempered by removal of the global-CA comparison and the new Section 4.2 numerical inconsistency: the cited noise-model rows differ by 0.46 dB, while the text claims 0.64 dB.
